note: tester.33 final component set. Each row records the exact source, recipe, architecture and flavour. The KMD, D3D12 shell, control app, state worker and desktop routers use b689e250, including catalog 55ac2dce and the compute/GDI settings. Router code and its recipe are unchanged from 37518825; the router rebuild is required by its embedded state-catalog identity. The D3D11 shell uses ce946478 (monitored-fence rewind flags). All Mesa rows include the GFX10 late-Z helper coverage repair, including coverage input retention and discard state. Hosted Mesa uses 39122af7 (validated target-independent rasterization with render targets, DirectMesh descriptor heap coexistence, ray-query CFG lifetime repair and accurate inverse trigonometric lowering), system x64 Mesa ad130cc2 (bounded diagnostic logging) and WOW64 20d7c8c9 (ray-query lifetime and inverse-trigonometric repairs, ABI preserved), and the D3D12 engine db6d7de0 with dxil-spirv fcd06d03 HitObject value semantics and exact native-half structured bounds/dimensions. The D3D12 shell uses 5aa711e5 for tight reserved-resource alignment and validated Generic Programs collection associations. Other component rows retain their individual pins. The x86/x64 system Vulkan difference is explained by the exact-pair note on the wow64 outputs. Data and third-party rows outside this build set remain in release-sources.json. All new bytes require the final installed-package gates before publication. Eight extra rows rebuild the caps/benchmark tools, H.264 MFT and HIP outputs for the current version instead of carrying tester.32 resources.

outputs.pair_skew: The x86 system Vulkan row remains on wow64 0aace3d3, with upstream Mesa a0ef4c88 merged. The x64 system row is aecf0012, which adds the BD-167 environment-read helper to 17b967ef. That change removes RADV_BC250_ACE_QUEUES lookup in the release flavour; an unset lab environment and the release default both follow the KMD compute-node capability. It does not port the x64 DXGI present or compute work to x86. The retained difference is deliberate: the BD-197 present route, BD-217 fix, compute queue and later x64 work have no measured x86 build. The x86 row passed the retained 864-case fill check; x64 still requires the final installed Vulkan and compute gates. Neither result proves feature parity. This note covers only 0aace3d3 and aecf0012 and must be reviewed when either pin changes.
